extracted.intended_audience: general readers, film enthusiasts, and researchers interested in the film Man on the Moon or Andy Kaufman
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or analyzing a feature-length biographical comedy-drama film (Man on the Moon) with attention to performance, historical fidelity, production choices, soundtrack, and reception. The page is an encyclopedic film article summarizing plot, production, accuracy issues, and critical/commercial response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical accuracy / factual fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: The film makes changes to Kaufman's life story; the prologue states: 'All the most important things in my life are changed around and mixed up for dramatic purposes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists concrete inaccuracies (e.g., the Carnegie Hall 'milk and cookies' performance portrayed as late in Kaufman's life though it occurred in 1979; misdating of SNL hosts; implying Taxi was canceled only once; Carol Kane's Taxi appearance timing). Critics and Kaufman's father complained that important parts of Andy's early life and career were omitted or misunderstood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-level accuracy vs dramatic extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy of individual scenes and sequence details (timing, participants, and duration) compared with real events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include prolonging the 'dead air' in the Mighty Mouse segment (in reality only a few seconds), depiction of an SNL vote sequence that actually occurred in a different year, and incorrect depiction of who hosted the first SNL episode. These illustrate the film's tendency to extend or reorder moments for drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capturing subject's persona and vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the film stays true to Kaufman's persona — his tendency to test, fool, deceive audiences and stage elaborate put-ons and hoaxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roger Ebert praised the film for remaining true to Kaufman's 'stubborn vision' and persona. The article highlights scenes (e.g., outrageous stunts, the wrestling feud, reading The Great Gatsby) that aim to convey Kaufman's approach to performance rather than strict biography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead performance authenticity and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The effectiveness and fidelity of the actor's portrayal of the real-life subject (Jim Carrey as Andy Kaufman).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes near-unanimous critical praise for Carrey's performance (Golden Globe win), and documents his 'rigid method acting' — staying in character on and off set — with examples (unscripted tics, Limburger cheese as Tony Clifton). The documentary Jim & Andy chronicles this approach and its impact on production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic license / narrative restructuring
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of creative license: changing sequence, mixing events, or ambiguously presenting events (e.g., whether Kaufman actually died).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The film's prologue admits mixing and changing facts for dramatic purposes; the movie deliberately leaves ambiguous whether Kaufman's death was real or a hoax. The historical-accuracy section and critics note where dramatic restructuring was used and sometimes criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production methods and actor approach (method acting)
rubrics_metrics.description: How production choices and actors' working methods (such as method acting) shape the film and its authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carrey's method acting (staying in character both on and off set) produced unscripted behaviors and on-set incidents (e.g., spat at Jerry Lawler, hospitalized after a physical altercation). The article references behind-the-scenes documentary footage highlighting these production dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting decisions and use of real-life cameos
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of actors for roles (including real-life figures) and inclusion of cameos by actual acquaintances or cast members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists principal casting (Carrey, DeVito, Courtney Love, Paul Giamatti) and many cameos by real-life friends and co-stars (David Letterman, Jerry Lawler, Taxi cast members). It also notes actors who auditioned (Kevin Spacey, Edward Norton, Nicolas Cage, John Cusack, Hank Azaria) and casting considerations (e.g., Disco Inferno considered for Lawler).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative focus and scope (which life aspects are highlighted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which periods, events, and aspects of the subject's life the film chooses to emphasize (e.g., comedy club beginnings, TV appearances, wrestling feud, Tony Clifton character).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article explains the film traces Kaufman's steps from childhood through his comedy-club and television appearances, focusing on inside jokes, scams, put-ons, and notably the Lawler feud and Tony Clifton. Critics complained about omitted material (e.g., early non-show-business life).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundtrack and title relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The contribution of soundtrack and title to the film's tone and marketing (R.E.M. wrote the soundtrack; the title comes from their song).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.E.M. composed the soundtrack; their 1992 song 'Man on the Moon' gave the film its title. The soundtrack included the Grammy-nominated 'The Great Beyond', noted as the band's highest-charting single in the UK, suggesting the music's role in the film's identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical and commercial reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured responses from critics, aggregators, audiences, awards bodies, and box office performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article provides specific metrics: Rotten Tomatoes 64% (122 critics, avg. rating 6.2/10), Metacritic score 58/100 (34 critics), CinemaScore average grade 'B−', Roger Ebert's 3.5/4 stars, Golden Globe win for Carrey, and box office gross of $47 million against a budget of $52–82 million. These are used to evaluate the film's overall success and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical/biographical sensitivity toward real people
rubrics_metrics.description: How the film handles portrayals of real people (family members, colleagues) and sensitive matters (e.g., illness, death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article reports that Kaufman's father and some critics were displeased with omissions and portrayals, and notes the film's ambiguous treatment of Kaufman's death, raising questions about ethical representation of real individuals and events.
